Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 43, verses 1–8:

Explanation of the words:

Ha Mim: This is one of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'a). It is written ḥā-mīm and read: Ḥā-Mīm.

Wal-Kitabi al-Mubin: That is, by the Qur'an which makes clear the path of guidance and the way of peace.

Inna ja'alnahu Qur'anan 'Arabiyyan: That is, We made it a Qur'an in the tongue of the Arabs, to be read in their language and understood through it.

La'allakum ta'qilun: That is, in hope that you, O Arabs, may understand what you are commanded and what you are forbidden.

Wa innahu fi Umm al-Kitab ladayna: That is, in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), the book of all decrees, which is with Us.

La'aliyyun hakim: That is, it is exalted and of high standing above the books before it, such that none can reach its level in its loftiness and elevation. Hakim: possessed of profound, lofty wisdom, the like of which cannot be attained.

Afanadribu 'ankumu al-dhikra safhan: Shall We then leave you alone and turn away the Reminder from you? That is, We will not send down the Qur'an concerning your commands, prohibitions, promises and threats.

An kuntum qawman musrifin: Because you are a people who exceed the limits in shirk and disbelief. No, We will not do so.

Wa kam arsalna min nabiyyin fi al-awwalin: That is, and We sent many prophets to the earlier generations of past nations.

Fa-ahlakna ashadda minhum batshan: That is, We sent Our punishment upon those stronger in might than your people, and destroyed them.

Wa mada mathalu al-awwalin: That is, the description of the destruction of the earlier peoples has passed in the Qur'anic verses.

Meaning of the verses:

Ha Mim: Allah knows best what He means by it. Wal-Kitabi al-Mubin: That is, by the Qur'an which makes clear everything that saves from the punishment of Allah and earns His Paradise and His pleasure. This is an oath which Allah swears, and what is sworn to is His saying: "Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an," that is, We made the Clear Book, which is the Qur'an, in Arabic, that is, in the tongue and language of the Arabs.

His saying, "that you may understand," explains the wisdom in making the Qur'an Arabic, that you may comprehend by observation and understand the purpose of Allah in what He sent down, regarding what He calls you to, so that acting upon it becomes easy for you, and you may be perfected and made happy. His saying, "And indeed it," that is, the Qur'an, "is in the Mother of the Book," that is, the Preserved Tablet, "with Us," that is, in Our presence, "is exalted," that is, of high standing and rank above all the books before it, "wise," that is, possessed of profound and lofty wisdom, the like of which cannot be attained.

His exalted saying: "Shall We then withhold the Reminder from you altogether, because you are a people who exceed the limits?" That is, shall We leave you in ignorance and turn away the Qur'an from you, so that you are not commanded or forbidden, because you are a people who exceed the limits in shirk, disbelief and denial? No, We will not do so. The interrogative here is for the purpose of rebuking them.

His saying, "And how many a prophet did We send among the earlier peoples?" That is, and We sent many prophets to the earlier nations, and no prophet came to them but they mocked him. That is, no messenger from Us came to any of those nations but they ridiculed him and scoffed at him, and at what he brought them of faith and monotheism, and at what he called them to of doing righteous deeds and abandoning what is forbidden. So be patient with your people, for they are following the path of those who came before them in disbelief, denial, ridicule and mockery.

His exalted saying: "Then We destroyed those who were stronger in might than them." That is, We destroyed those in those past nations who were stronger in might, when they denied Our messengers and mocked them. How then (would it be) with these people, who are weaker and less powerful than they? It is more fitting that they should not escape Our punishment whenever We wish to send it upon them.

His saying, "And the example of the earlier peoples has passed." That is, the description of the destruction of the earlier peoples has passed in the Qur'anic verses, such as the people of 'Ad, Thamud, the companions of Madyan, and the overturned cities. Was there not in that a lesson for your people, if they would take heed?

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The legitimacy of swearing by Allah, the Exalted.

2- Explanation of the nobility of the Noble Qur'an and its high station above all previous books.

3- That people being excessive in shirk and corruption does not prevent their admonition, advice and guidance.

4- Explanation of a human custom: that no messenger came to them but they mocked him.

5- In the destruction of the stronger is evidence that destroying one who is lesser is more fitting and more deserving, especially with the intensity of his disbelief.

Meaning of the verses:

Ha Mim: Allah knows best what He means by it. Wal-Kitabi al-Mubin: That is, by the Qur'an which makes clear everything that saves from the punishment of Allah and earns His Paradise and His pleasure. This is an oath which Allah swears, and what is sworn to is His saying: "Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an," that is, We made the Clear Book, which is the Qur'an, in Arabic, that is, in the tongue and language of the Arabs.

His saying, "that you may understand," explains the wisdom in making the Qur'an Arabic, that you may comprehend by observation and understand the purpose of Allah in what He sent down, regarding what He calls you to, so that acting upon it becomes easy for you, and you may be perfected and made happy. His saying, "And indeed it," that is, the Qur'an, "is in the Mother of the Book," that is, the Preserved Tablet, "with Us," that is, in Our presence, "is exalted," that is, of high standing and rank above all the books before it, "wise," that is, possessed of profound and lofty wisdom, the like of which cannot be attained.

His exalted saying: "Shall We then withhold the Reminder from you altogether, because you are a people who exceed the limits?" That is, shall We leave you in ignorance and turn away the Qur'an from you, so that you are not commanded or forbidden, because you are a people who exceed the limits in shirk, disbelief and denial? No, We will not do so. The interrogative here is for the purpose of rebuking them.

His saying, "And how many a prophet did We send among the earlier peoples?" That is, and We sent many prophets to the earlier nations, and no prophet came to them but they mocked him. That is, no messenger from Us came to any of those nations but they ridiculed him and scoffed at him, and at what he brought them of faith and monotheism, and at what he called them to of doing righteous deeds and abandoning what is forbidden. So be patient with your people, for they are following the path of those who came before them in disbelief, denial, ridicule and mockery.

His exalted saying: "Then We destroyed those who were stronger in might than them." That is, We destroyed those in those past nations who were stronger in might, when they denied Our messengers and mocked them. How then (would it be) with these people, who are weaker and less powerful than they? It is more fitting that they should not escape Our punishment whenever We wish to send it upon them.

His saying, "And the example of the earlier peoples has passed." That is, the description of the destruction of the earlier peoples has passed in the Qur'anic verses, such as the people of 'Ad, Thamud, the companions of Madyan, and the overturned cities. Was there not in that a lesson for your people, if they would take heed?

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

2- Explanation of the nobility of the Noble Qur'an and its high station above all previous books.

3- That people being excessive in shirk and corruption does not prevent their admonition, advice and guidance.

4- Explanation of a human custom: that no messenger came to them but they mocked him.

5- In the destruction of the stronger is evidence that destroying one who is lesser is more fitting and more deserving, especially with the intensity of his disbelief.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 43, verses 9–14:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Wa-la-in sa'altahum﴾: that is, "and if you were to ask these polytheists of your people, O our Messenger."

﴿Man khalaqa al-samawati wal-ard﴾: that is, who began the creation of them and brought them into being? They would surely say, "God created them, the Mighty, the All-Knowing."

﴿Alladhi ja'ala lakumu al-arda mahdan﴾: that is, God, who made the earth for you a bed, like a cradle for a child.

﴿Wa-ja'ala lakum fiha subulan﴾: that is, roads.

﴿La'allakum tahtadun﴾: that is, so that you may reach your destinations on your journeys.

﴿Ma'an biqadar﴾: that is, in measure according to need, and He did not make it a flood that drowns and destroys.

﴿Fa-ansharna bihi baldatan maytan﴾: that is, so We gave life with it to a dead town, having no plants or crops.

﴿Kadhalika tukhrajun﴾: that is, just as this giving of life to the dead earth by water happens, you too will be brought to life and come out of your graves.

﴿Wal-ladhi khalaqa al-azwaja kullaha﴾: that is, who created every thing, since all things are paired and no single thing is known to be unpaired except God.

﴿Wa-ja'ala lakum min al-fulki wal-an'ami﴾: that is, ships and camels.

﴿Li-tastawu ala zuhurihi﴾: that is, that you may settle upon the backs of what you ride.

﴿Wa-ma kunna lahu muqrinin﴾: that is, capable of controlling them and not subduing them.

﴿Wa-inna ila rabbina lamunqalibun﴾: that is, we shall surely return to Him.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in calling the polytheists to monotheism with the words of the Most High: ﴿And if you were to ask them﴾, that is, if you were to ask these polytheists of your people, O our Messenger, "Who created the heavens and the earth?", that is, who originated and brought them into being after non-existence, they would hasten to answer, "God," yet despite their acknowledgment of His lordship over everything, they associate idols and images in His worship. In other verses they explicitly named the Majestic Name, God; and in this verse they said: "the Mighty, the All-Knowing," that is, God, whose might cannot be challenged and whose knowledge cannot be encompassed. The words of the Most High: ﴿Who made the earth for you a bed﴾, that is, a spread and a carpet like a child's cradle, and this is the speech of God Most High, not of the polytheists, since their speech ended at "the Mighty, the All-Knowing." When they described Him with the two attributes of might and knowledge, it was appropriate to mention other sublime attributes to make Him known to them, so the Most High said: ﴿Who made the earth for you a bed﴾, that is, a spread and carpet, and made for you therein roads, that is, paths, so that you may reach your destinations to attain your needs in the lands here and there. And He who sends down water from the sky in measure, which is rain in measured quantities according to need, so it is neither shallow and scanty, benefiting nothing, nor a flood that drowns and destroys. The words ﴿So We gave life﴾ mean that by that rain We revived a town, that is, dry land with no plants or crops. The words ﴿Thus you will be brought forth﴾ mean that just as the dead earth is revived, He, the Most High, will give you life and bring you forth from your graves alive.

The words ﴿And He who created all pairs﴾ are another description of Him, that He created all pairs: male and female, good and evil, health and sickness, justice and injustice, since no single thing is unpaired except Him, glory be to Him and exalted. In the authentic hadith: "God is Witr (one) and loves the odd (Witr)," and: "Say: He is God, the One." The words ﴿And made for you of the ships and cattle that you ride﴾ are another description by His acts, which indicate His existence, power and knowledge and necessitate His divinity, since He made for people ships, that is, vessels to ride, and from cattle such as camels, and from beasts such as horses, mules and donkeys likewise. The words ﴿That you may settle upon their backs﴾ mean that you may be settled upon their backs, that is, the backs of what you ride; then you remember your Lord's blessing in your hearts when you are mounted, and say with your tongues: "Glory be to the One who has subjected this to us; and we could never have controlled it, nor are we capable of it by ourselves," that is, God has made it subservient to us and enabled us to control it; ﴿And we could never have controlled it﴾, that is, that riding animal, by subduing it, due to our weakness and its strength; ﴿And indeed to our Lord we shall surely return﴾, that is, we shall surely return to Him after our death.

Guidance of the verses:

1. Establishing tawhid by mentioning the attributes of lordship, which necessitate worship of Him alone.
2. Affirming the doctrine of resurrection and recompense.
3. The miracle of the Qur'an in informing of pairing, and modern science has established the principle of pairing, even in the atom, which consists of positive and negative charges.
4. The legitimacy of saying the name of God and remembrance when riding what is ridden: if it is a ship or car, one says "In the name of God be its course and its anchoring; indeed my Lord is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful"; if it is an animal, one says at the start "In the name of God," and when seated upon it: "Glory be to the One who has subjected this to us, and we could never have controlled it, and to our Lord we shall surely return."

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 43, verse 15–23:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And they have made of His servants a part of Him﴾: That is, those polytheists, who acknowledge that Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth, made of His servants a part of Him, when they said the angels are the daughters of Allah.

﴿Indeed, mankind is clearly ungrateful﴾: That is, indeed this human being, who acknowledges that Allah created the heavens and made of His servants a part of Him, is clearly ungrateful, meaning exceedingly disbelieving in a manifest way.

﴿And has chosen for Himself daughters over sons?﴾: That is, He singled you out with sons and chose them exclusively for you.

﴿For what he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness﴾: That is, for what they ascribed to the Most Merciful as a likeness, which is offspring.

﴿His face becomes dark, and he is filled with suppressed grief﴾: That is, he remains the whole day with a face darkened by sorrow, and is full of rage.

﴿Is one who is brought up among ornaments [and is weak in argument]?﴾: That is, do they dare against Allah and attribute to Him a part, namely daughters, who are raised in adornment?

﴿And is not clear in dispute﴾: That is, one who does not express a proof, because of their weakness in femininity.

﴿Who made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females﴾: That is, because they said the angels are the daughters of Allah.

﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾: That is, were they present at their creation when the Most Merciful was creating them?

﴿Their testimony will be recorded﴾: That is, their statement that the angels are female will be recorded.

﴿And they will be questioned﴾: That is, on the Day of Resurrection they will be questioned about their false testimonies and punished for them.

﴿They have no knowledge of that﴾: That is, their claim that Allah is pleased with their worship of the angels has no evidence or knowledge behind it.

﴿They are only guessing﴾: That is, they are only lying, inheriting ignorance from one another.

﴿Or have We given them a Book before this, so they are holding to it?﴾: That is, or have We sent down to them a Book before the Qur'an?

﴿Rather, they say, "We found our fathers upon a religion"﴾: That is, they have no proof except blind imitation of their fathers.

﴿And we are following in their footsteps﴾: That is, we walk in their path and creed, and that is the worship of other than Allah, such as angels and others, and idols and images.

﴿Nor did We send before you any warner to a city but its affluent said﴾: That is, its wealthy people, those enjoying the luxury of life.

﴿"We found our fathers upon a religion"﴾: That is, a creed and a faith.

﴿"And we are following in their footsteps"﴾: That is, we follow them in their path.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in calling the polytheists to monotheism and the deniers to belief. Allah, the Exalted, says, denouncing their falsehood and rebuking them for holding and asserting it: ﴿And they have made of His servants a part of Him﴾, that is, those ignorant polytheists made for Allah a portion of His creation, when they said the angels are the daughters of Allah. This is among the greatest lies and the greatest disbelief. For how did they know that the angels are female, that they are the daughters of Allah, and that they deserve worship alongside Allah, so that they worshipped them? Indeed, ﴿mankind is clearly ungrateful﴾, that is, exceedingly disbelieving, and its clear disbelief needs no proof. And His saying: ﴿Has He chosen daughters over what He creates and singled you out with sons?﴾, that is: do you say, O polytheists who fabricate, that Allah has taken daughters from among what He creates, and singled you out with sons? The meaning is that He preferred you for Himself with males, whom you love, and was content for Himself with females, whom you hate. How strange is this corrupt understanding of yours.

As for His saying: ﴿And when one of them is given good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness, his face becomes dark and he is filled with suppressed grief﴾, that is: these who ascribe daughters to Allah falsely and fabricatedly, when one of them has a daughter born to him and is given the news, that his wife has borne a daughter, his face remains darkened all day from distress and grief, and he is full of suppressed sorrow and anguish.

As for His saying: ﴿Is one who is brought up among ornaments, and in dispute is not clear?﴾, Allah denounces them and rebukes them for their lies and their poor understanding, saying: do they dare, and reach the extreme of bad manners, and attribute to Allah one who is raised in adornment because of her deficiency, namely daughters, who in dispute is not clear because of the weakness of her intellect? Until it was said: no woman ever argued a proof except that it turned against her, not for her. So His saying ﴿not clear in dispute﴾ means not expressing a proof because of her weakness by nature, which is femaleness. The pronoun refers to the one in His saying ﴿one who is brought up among ornaments﴾, that is, adornment.

As for His saying: ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females﴾, that is, when they said the angels are the daughters of Allah, and worshipped them for that, seeking their intercession and benefit from their worship. Allah, the Exalted, said, rebuking them and establishing proof against their lies: ﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾, that is, were they present at their creation when Allah was creating them? The answer is no. From where would they have that, when they had not yet been created, nor their fathers, nor even Adam, their origin, peace be upon him? And His saying: ﴿Their testimony will be recorded﴾, this being their statement that the angels are the daughters of Allah, and they will be questioned about it, held to account, and punished for it with the most severe kinds of punishment, because it is falsehood and fabrication, and "upon" [i.e., "ʿalā" in the sense of "about"]: it is upon Allah, we seek refuge in Allah. And His saying: ﴿And they say, "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them."﴾ That is, those polytheistic fabricators said to whoever denounced their worship of the angels and other idols: if the Most Merciful had willed that we not worship them, we would not have worshipped them. Allah said in refutation of them: ﴿They have no knowledge of that﴾, that is, they have no knowledge whatsoever that Allah is pleased with their worship of them. In their saying that, they are only guessing, that is, speaking by conjecture and falsehood, since knowledge comes through a Book or a Prophet, and they have neither a Book nor a Prophet among them who said this. Therefore Allah, denouncing their wicked saying, says: ﴿Or have We given them a Book before this, so they are holding to it?﴾ No, no. Allah has not given them any Book, nor has any warner come to them before Muhammad. So they have no proof except the blind imitation of fathers and forefathers, who were ignorant and astray. This is what Allah related of them in His saying: ﴿Rather, they say, "We found our fathers upon a religion," that is, a creed, ﴿and we are following in their footsteps, guided﴾, that is, walking, following their traces. And His saying: ﴿And similarly, We did not send before you any warner to a city but its affluent said﴾, that is, any messenger, ﴿"We found our fathers upon a religion," that is, a creed and a faith, ﴿"and we are following in their footsteps," that is, following them in it. This is the custom of the nations before your nation, O Our Messenger, so do not grieve over them, nor be in distress over what they say, believe, and do.

This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And similarly, We did not send before you﴾ to the end of the verse.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of a trait of man before he is healed by faith and worship, which is clear and manifest disbelief.

2- The obligation to denounce evil and to try to change it within the bounds the Law permits and human capacity allows.

3- Explanation of the state of the Arab polytheists in the Jahiliyyah, in their dislike of daughters out of fear of shame, and that was due to their intense jealousy.

4- Explanation of the weakness and deficiency of women, which is why they are completed through adornment, and that the deficiency in them is innate in both body and mind.

5- Explanation that whoever speaks a statement or gives a false testimony will be questioned about it on the Day of Resurrection and punished for it.

6- The prohibition of speaking about Allah without knowledge, so it is not permissible to attribute to Allah the Exalted anything He has not attributed to Himself.

7- The prohibition of blind imitation of fathers, people of the lands, and shaykhs, so no statement is accepted except with evidence from the Law.

Allah, the Exalted, said, rebuking them and establishing proof against their lies: ﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾, that is, were they present at their creation when Allah was creating them? The answer is no. From where would they have that, when they had not yet been created, nor their fathers, nor even Adam, their origin, peace be upon him? And His saying: ﴿Their testimony will be recorded﴾, this being their statement that the angels are the daughters of Allah, and they will be questioned about it, held to account, and punished for it with the most severe kinds of punishment, because it is falsehood and fabrication, and "upon" [i.e., "ʿalā" in the sense of "about"]: it is upon Allah, we seek refuge in Allah. And His saying: ﴿And they say, "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them."﴾ That is, those polytheistic fabricators said to whoever denounced their worship of the angels and other idols: if the Most Merciful had willed that we not worship them, we would not have worshipped them. Allah said in refutation of them: ﴿They have no knowledge of that﴾, that is, they have no knowledge whatsoever that Allah is pleased with their worship of them. In their saying that, they are only guessing, that is, speaking by conjecture and falsehood, since knowledge comes through a Book or a Prophet, and they have neither a Book nor a Prophet among them who said this. Therefore Allah, denouncing their wicked saying, says: ﴿Or have We given them a Book before this, so they are holding to it?﴾ No, no. Allah has not given them any Book, nor has any warner come to them before Muhammad. So they have no proof except the blind imitation of fathers and forefathers, who were ignorant and astray. This is what Allah related of them in His saying: ﴿Rather, they say, "We found our fathers upon a religion," that is, a creed, ﴿and we are following in their footsteps, guided﴾, that is, walking, following their traces. And His saying: ﴿And similarly, We did not send before you any warner to a city but its affluent said﴾, that is, any messenger, ﴿"We found our fathers upon a religion," that is, a creed and a faith, ﴿"and we are following in their footsteps," that is, following them in it. This is the custom of the nations before your nation, O Our Messenger, so do not grieve over them, nor be in distress over what they say, believe, and do.

This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And similarly, We did not send before you﴾ to the end of the verse.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of a trait of man before he is healed by faith and worship, which is clear and manifest disbelief.

2- The obligation to denounce evil and to try to change it within the bounds the Law permits and human capacity allows.

3- Explanation of the state of the Arab polytheists in the Jahiliyyah, in their dislike of daughters out of fear of shame, and that was due to their intense jealousy.

4- Explanation of the weakness and deficiency of women, which is why they are completed through adornment, and that the deficiency in them is innate in both body and mind.

5- Explanation that whoever speaks a statement or gives a false testimony will be questioned about it on the Day of Resurrection and punished for it.

6- The prohibition of speaking about Allah without knowledge, so it is not permissible to attribute to Allah the Exalted anything He has not attributed to Himself.

7- The prohibition of blind imitation of fathers, people of the lands, and shaykhs, so no statement is accepted except with evidence from the Law.

**Explanation of the words:**

*"Qal awa law ji'tukum bi-ahda mimma wajadtum 'alayhi aba'akum"* (Their messenger said: "Even if I brought you something better guided than what you found your fathers upon?"): Their messenger said to them: "Do you follow your fathers, even if I brought you something better than what you found your fathers upon, that is, better guidance to the truth, to happiness and to perfection?"

*"Qalu inna bima ursiltum bihi kafirun"* (They said: "Indeed we disbelieve in what you have been sent with"): That is, the polytheists said to their messengers in reply: "Indeed we disbelieve in what you were sent with," that is, we deny it and reject it, not acknowledging it.

*"Fa-unzur kayfa kana 'aqibatu al-mukadhdhibin"* (So look at how was the end of the deniers): That is, it was destruction and ruin. Therefore, O our Messenger, do not be concerned about the denial of your people.

*"Wa-idh qala Ibrahim"* (And when Abraham said): That is, and mention when Abraham, the father of the prophets, the Friend of the Most Merciful (*khalil al-Rahman*), said.

*"Inni bara'un mimma ta'budun"* (Indeed, I am free from what you worship): That is, I am free from what you worship of idols; I do not worship them and I do not acknowledge them.

*"Illa alladhi fataranī fa-innahu sa-yahdin"* (Except He who originated me, for indeed He will guide me): That is, but I worship the One who created me and I acknowledge Him, for He will guide me, that is, He will direct me to what perfects me and makes me happy in the worldly life and in the Hereafter.

*"Wa-ja'alaha kalimatan baqiyatan fi 'aqibihi"* (And He made it a word that remains among his descendants): That is, Abraham made the word of *tawhid* (the affirmation of God's oneness), "*la ilaha illa Allah*" (There is no god but Allah), lasting and enduring among his offspring, for he enjoined it upon them, as Allah the Exalted said: "And Abraham instructed his sons with it" (2:132).

*"La'allahum yarji'un"* (That perhaps they might return): That is, in hope that they would repent to Allah and return to His tawhid whenever they remember it, which is "*la ilaha illa Allah*."

*"Bal matta'tuha'ula'i wa-aba'ahum"* (Rather, I gave enjoyment to these and their fathers): That is, these polytheists and their fathers, by granting them life, so I did not hasten punishment upon them.

*"Hatta ja'ahumu al-haqqu wa-rasulun mubin"* (Until there came to them the truth and a clear messenger): That is, until the Qur'an came carrying the true religion, and a clear messenger, whose mission is beyond doubt, and he is Muhammad (ﷺ), who makes clear to them the path of guidance and the legal rulings (*ahkam shar'iyyah*).

*"Wa-qalu lawla nuzzila hadha al-Qur'anu 'ala rajulin mina al-qaryatayni 'azim"* (And they said: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from the two cities?"): That is, these polytheists, whom We granted life without punishing them, said: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon one of two men from the two cities of Makkah and al-Ta'if?", namely al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah in Makkah or 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi in al-Ta'if.

*"A-hum yaqsimuna rahmata rabbik?"* (Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?): That is, Allah the Exalted denies them this arbitrary presumption and false suggestion, saying: "Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?", since prophethood is among the greatest mercies. And they have no right to appoint anyone as a prophet, for this belongs to Allah alone.

*"Nahnu qasamna baynahum ma'ishatahum fi al-hayat al-dunya"* (We have distributed among them their livelihood in the worldly life): That is, since We are the ones who distribute their livelihood among them, making one rich and another poor, granting this one wealth and restricting that one, how then can prophethood, which is more sublime and precious than food and drink, be left to them? We have more right to it than they do, so We appoint as prophet whom We will.

*"Liyattakhidha ba'dahum ba'dan sukhriyyan"* (So that some of them may take others in service): That is, We made this one rich and that one poor so that the rich would take the poor as servants to serve them, hired for wages in return for their labour.

*"Wa-rahmatu rabbika khayrun mimma yajma'un"* (And the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate): That is, the Garden which Allah has prepared for you and for your followers is better than the wealth which these disbelieving polytheists gather.

**The meaning of the verses:**

When the Exalted mentioned the saying of the polytheists to their messengers: "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion (*ummah*, 'community/creed'), and indeed we are following in their footsteps" (43:22), He related, informing of the words of the Messenger to his deniers, who imitate their fathers, the wrongdoers: "Say: 'Even if I brought you something better guided than what you found your fathers upon?'" That is: Do you follow your fathers and not follow me? Even if I brought you something better, leading to good and happiness, than what you found your fathers upon. This is a denunciation from the Messenger against them in the form of a question, and it is also a rebuke, for the rational person follows guidance, whoever brings it, whether near or far.

His saying, the Exalted: "They said: 'Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent'" (43:24) is the saying of the denying, polytheistic nations to their messengers, meaning that every nation said this to its messenger: "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with," of tawhid, the belief in resurrection and recompense, and the Law and its rulings, that is, we deny it and reject it, not affirming it. The Exalted said: "So We took vengeance upon them" (43:25), that is, for their denial, We destroyed them. "So look, O our Messenger, at how was the end of those who denied," it was a total destruction and complete ruin. Let your people be reminded of this, that perhaps they may remember.

His saying, the Exalted: "And when Abraham said to his father and his people, 'Indeed, I am free from what you worship'" (43:26–27): That is, mention, O our Messenger, to your people the saying of Abraham, to whom they falsely attribute themselves, to his father and his people: "Indeed, I am free from what you worship," that is, I am free from your gods that you worship, so I do not worship them and I do not acknowledge their worship. His saying "Except He who originated me" means: but worship Allah who created me, for He is more deserving of worship than what did not create me and created nothing, while itself being created. His saying "for indeed He will guide me" means He will always guide me to what is in my happiness and perfection.

His saying, the Exalted: "And He made it a word that remains among his descendants, so that they might return" (43:28): That is, and his disavowal of shirk (associating others with God) and the polytheists, and his worship being exclusively for Allah, Lord of the worlds, he made it a lasting word among his descendants, since he enjoined it upon them, as is mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah where He said: "And Abraham instructed his sons with it" (2:132), that is, that they should not worship except Allah. So it is the word "*la ilaha illa Allah*" which Abraham bequeathed to his children, so that they might return to it whenever they become heedless, forgetful and abandon the worship of Allah the Exalted and turning to Him, under the influences of evil and corruption from the devils of mankind and jinn. Then they remember and repent to Allah the Exalted, so they affirm His oneness and worship Him. May Allah reward Abraham on behalf of the believers with goodness.

His saying, the Exalted: "Rather, I gave enjoyment to these and their fathers until there came to them the truth and a clear messenger" (43:29): That is, rather, what Abraham hoped for was not fully realised when some of his descendants committed shirk, including these polytheists contemporary with you, O Messenger, and their fathers. And I granted them life until there came to them the truth, which is this Qur'an, recited by this clear Messenger, that is, the one who clarifies all the rulings and explains all the laws. When the truth came to them they said: "This is magic, and indeed we disbelieve in it." Thus said Quraysh when the truth came to them, which is the Qur'an bearing the laws and rulings, and the Messenger who clarifies and explains it. They said: "This is magic which bewitches us," "and indeed we disbelieve in it," that is, in the Qur'an and the Messenger, we deny and reject and disbelieve.

They went further into error and confusion, which the Exalted related about them in His saying: "And they said: 'Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from the two cities?'" (43:31), that is: Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a noble man of standing, such as al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah in Makkah or 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud in al-Ta'if? This is a purely material outlook, since they saw that nobility lies in wealth, and since Muhammad (ﷺ) had no property or riches, they saw that he was not fit for prophethood nor for being followed in it. So the Exalted refuted their base materialistic view with His saying: "Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?" (43:32). Are they not ashamed, when they say: "Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord," giving from it to whom they wish and withholding from whom they wish? Or are We the distributors? "We have distributed among them their livelihood," their food, drink, clothing, dwelling and means of transport, in the worldly life. Then how can one who is incapable even of feeding, watering and clothing himself not be ashamed to object to Allah in His choice of the one who is fit for His prophethood and message?

His saying, the Exalted: "And We raised some of them above others in degrees" (43:32): That is, in provision, so this one is rich and that one is poor, so that the poor may serve the rich. This is the meaning of His saying: "So that some of them may take others in service," for if they were all rich, no one would serve anyone and life would come to a halt. His saying: "And the mercy of your Lord" means the Garden, the Abode of Peace, "is better than what they accumulate of wealth," wealth whose possessors they preferred, even though they were among the lowest of people in rank and the least in nobility.

They saw that they were more deserving of prophethood than you, because their souls were diseased with love of wealth and desires.

**The guidance from the verses:**

1- It is part of intellectual perfection that a person follows guidance even if his people and the people of his land oppose it.

2- It is obligatory to disavow shirk and the polytheists, and this is the meaning of "*la ilaha illa Allah*."

3- The virtue of one who bequeaths guidance and righteousness to his children.

4- No one may object to Allah in His law and His management except that he disbelieves, and we seek refuge in Allah the Exalted.

5- Clarification of the wisdom in wealth and poverty, health and sickness, intelligence and dullness.

*"Qal awa law ji'tukum bi-ahda mimma wajadtum 'alayhi aba'akum"* (Their messenger said: "Even if I brought you something better guided than what you found your fathers upon?"): Their messenger said to them: "Do you follow your fathers, even if I brought you something better than what you found your fathers upon, that is, better guidance to the truth, to happiness and to perfection?"

*"Qalu inna bima ursiltum bihi kafirun"* (They said: "Indeed we disbelieve in what you have been sent with"): That is, the polytheists said to their messengers in reply: "Indeed we disbelieve in what you were sent with," that is, we deny it and reject it, not acknowledging it.

*"Fa-unzur kayfa kana 'aqibatu al-mukadhdhibin"* (So look at how was the end of the deniers): That is, it was destruction and ruin. Therefore, O our Messenger, do not be concerned about the denial of your people.

*"Wa-idh qala Ibrahim"* (And when Abraham said): That is, and mention when Abraham, the father of the prophets, the Friend of the Most Merciful (*khalil al-Rahman*), said.

*"Inni bara'un mimma ta'budun"* (Indeed, I am free from what you worship): That is, I am free from what you worship of idols; I do not worship them and I do not acknowledge them.

*"Illa alladhi fataranī fa-innahu sa-yahdin"* (Except He who originated me, for indeed He will guide me): That is, but I worship the One who created me and I acknowledge Him, for He will guide me, that is, He will direct me to what perfects me and makes me happy in the worldly life and in the Hereafter.

*"Wa-ja'alaha kalimatan baqiyatan fi 'aqibihi"* (And He made it a word that remains among his descendants): That is, Abraham made the word of *tawhid* (the affirmation of God's oneness), "*la ilaha illa Allah*" (There is no god but Allah), lasting and enduring among his offspring, for he enjoined it upon them, as Allah the Exalted said: "And Abraham instructed his sons with it" (2:132).

*"La'allahum yarji'un"* (That perhaps they might return): That is, in hope that they would repent to Allah and return to His tawhid whenever they remember it, which is "*la ilaha illa Allah*."

*"Bal matta'tuha'ula'i wa-aba'ahum"* (Rather, I gave enjoyment to these and their fathers): That is, these polytheists and their fathers, by granting them life, so I did not hasten punishment upon them.

*"Hatta ja'ahumu al-haqqu wa-rasulun mubin"* (Until there came to them the truth and a clear messenger): That is, until the Qur'an came carrying the true religion, and a clear messenger, whose mission is beyond doubt, and he is Muhammad (ﷺ), who makes clear to them the path of guidance and the legal rulings (*ahkam shar'iyyah*).

*"Wa-qalu lawla nuzzila hadha al-Qur'anu 'ala rajulin mina al-qaryatayni 'azim"* (And they said: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from the two cities?"): That is, these polytheists, whom We granted life without punishing them, said: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon one of two men from the two cities of Makkah and al-Ta'if?", namely al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah in Makkah or 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi in al-Ta'if.

*"A-hum yaqsimuna rahmata rabbik?"* (Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?): That is, Allah the Exalted denies them this arbitrary presumption and false suggestion, saying: "Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?", since prophethood is among the greatest mercies. And they have no right to appoint anyone as a prophet, for this belongs to Allah alone.

*"Nahnu qasamna baynahum ma'ishatahum fi al-hayat al-dunya"* (We have distributed among them their livelihood in the worldly life): That is, since We are the ones who distribute their livelihood among them, making one rich and another poor, granting this one wealth and restricting that one, how then can prophethood, which is more sublime and precious than food and drink, be left to them? We have more right to it than they do, so We appoint as prophet whom We will.

*"Liyattakhidha ba'dahum ba'dan sukhriyyan"* (So that some of them may take others in service): That is, We made this one rich and that one poor so that the rich would take the poor as servants to serve them, hired for wages in return for their labour.

*"Wa-rahmatu rabbika khayrun mimma yajma'un"* (And the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate): That is, the Garden which Allah has prepared for you and for your followers is better than the wealth which these disbelieving polytheists gather.

**The meaning of the verses:**

When the Exalted mentioned the saying of the polytheists to their messengers: "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion (*ummah*, 'community/creed'), and indeed we are following in their footsteps" (43:22), He related, informing of the words of the Messenger to his deniers, who imitate their fathers, the wrongdoers: "Say: 'Even if I brought you something better guided than what you found your fathers upon?'" That is: Do you follow your fathers and not follow me? Even if I brought you something better, leading to good and happiness, than what you found your fathers upon. This is a denunciation from the Messenger against them in the form of a question, and it is also a rebuke, for the rational person follows guidance, whoever brings it, whether near or far.

His saying, the Exalted: "They said: 'Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent'" (43:24) is the saying of the denying, polytheistic nations to their messengers, meaning that every nation said this to its messenger: "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with," of tawhid, the belief in resurrection and recompense, and the Law and its rulings, that is, we deny it and reject it, not affirming it. The Exalted said: "So We took vengeance upon them" (43:25), that is, for their denial, We destroyed them. "So look, O our Messenger, at how was the end of those who denied," it was a total destruction and complete ruin. Let your people be reminded of this, that perhaps they may remember.

His saying, the Exalted: "And when Abraham said to his father and his people, 'Indeed, I am free from what you worship'" (43:26–27): That is, mention, O our Messenger, to your people the saying of Abraham, to whom they falsely attribute themselves, to his father and his people: "Indeed, I am free from what you worship," that is, I am free from your gods that you worship, so I do not worship them and I do not acknowledge their worship. His saying "Except He who originated me" means: but worship Allah who created me, for He is more deserving of worship than what did not create me and created nothing, while itself being created. His saying "for indeed He will guide me" means He will always guide me to what is in my happiness and perfection.

His saying, the Exalted: "And He made it a word that remains among his descendants, so that they might return" (43:28): That is, and his disavowal of shirk (associating others with God) and the polytheists, and his worship being exclusively for Allah, Lord of the worlds, he made it a lasting word among his descendants, since he enjoined it upon them, as is mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah where He said: "And Abraham instructed his sons with it" (2:132), that is, that they should not worship except Allah. So it is the word "*la ilaha illa Allah*" which Abraham bequeathed to his children, so that they might return to it whenever they become heedless, forgetful and abandon the worship of Allah the Exalted and turning to Him, under the influences of evil and corruption from the devils of mankind and jinn. Then they remember and repent to Allah the Exalted, so they affirm His oneness and worship Him. May Allah reward Abraham on behalf of the believers with goodness.

His saying, the Exalted: "Rather, I gave enjoyment to these and their fathers until there came to them the truth and a clear messenger" (43:29): That is, rather, what Abraham hoped for was not fully realised when some of his descendants committed shirk, including these polytheists contemporary with you, O Messenger, and their fathers. And I granted them life until there came to them the truth, which is this Qur'an, recited by this clear Messenger, that is, the one who clarifies all the rulings and explains all the laws. When the truth came to them they said: "This is magic, and indeed we disbelieve in it." Thus said Quraysh when the truth came to them, which is the Qur'an bearing the laws and rulings, and the Messenger who clarifies and explains it. They said: "This is magic which bewitches us," "and indeed we disbelieve in it," that is, in the Qur'an and the Messenger, we deny and reject and disbelieve.

They went further into error and confusion, which the Exalted related about them in His saying: "And they said: 'Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from the two cities?'" (43:31), that is: Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a noble man of standing, such as al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah in Makkah or 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud in al-Ta'if? This is a purely material outlook, since they saw that nobility lies in wealth, and since Muhammad (ﷺ) had no property or riches, they saw that he was not fit for prophethood nor for being followed in it. So the Exalted refuted their base materialistic view with His saying: "Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?" (43:32). Are they not ashamed, when they say: "Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord," giving from it to whom they wish and withholding from whom they wish? Or are We the distributors? "We have distributed among them their livelihood," their food, drink, clothing, dwelling and means of transport, in the worldly life. Then how can one who is incapable even of feeding, watering and clothing himself not be ashamed to object to Allah in His choice of the one who is fit for His prophethood and message?

His saying, the Exalted: "And We raised some of them above others in degrees" (43:32): That is, in provision, so this one is rich and that one is poor, so that the poor may serve the rich. This is the meaning of His saying: "So that some of them may take others in service," for if they were all rich, no one would serve anyone and life would come to a halt. His saying: "And the mercy of your Lord" means the Garden, the Abode of Peace, "is better than what they accumulate of wealth," wealth whose possessors they preferred, even though they were among the lowest of people in rank and the least in nobility.

They saw that they were more deserving of prophethood than you, because their souls were diseased with love of wealth and desires.

**The guidance from the verses:**

1- It is part of intellectual perfection that a person follows guidance even if his people and the people of his land oppose it.

2- It is obligatory to disavow shirk and the polytheists, and this is the meaning of "*la ilaha illa Allah*."

3- The virtue of one who bequeaths guidance and righteousness to his children.

4- No one may object to Allah in His law and His management except that he disbelieves, and we seek refuge in Allah the Exalted.

5- Clarification of the wisdom in wealth and poverty, health and sickness, intelligence and dullness.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 43, verses 33–35:

Explanation of the words:

*Ummah wahidah* (a single community): that is, upon disbelief.

*Ma'arij* (ascending stairways): like ladders and modern elevators; *ma'arij* is the plural of *mu'arraj*, which means an ascending device.

*Ya'zharun 'alayha* (they could ascend upon them): that is, they could climb up on them to the rooftops.

*Zukhrufan* (adornment): that is, gold. Meaning: We would have made roofs of silver and gold for their houses, and likewise the doors, the stairways, and the couches, some of them of silver and some of them of gold.

*Wa inna kullu dhalika* (and all of that): that is, all that has been mentioned.

*Lamma mata'u al-hayat al-dunya* (merely the enjoyment of the life of this world): that is, all of that is nothing but the enjoyment of the life of this world, which one enjoys in it and then it passes away.

*Wal-akhirah* (and the Hereafter): that is, Paradise and its bounties, which are better for the people of faith and piety than the enjoyments of this world.

Meaning of the verses:

When the Exalted had given preference to Paradise over wealth and worldly goods in the previous verses, He said here: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community﴾, that is, upon disbelief, We would have given those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful (meaning Himself, Mighty and Majestic) roofs of silver for their houses, and ascending stairways upon which they would climb to the upper chambers and rooftops, of silver. And We would likewise have given their houses doors and couches upon which they recline, also of silver, and *zukhrufan*, that is, gold: some of what has been mentioned of silver and some of gold, so that it would be more beautiful and splendid than silver alone. ﴿And all of that is nothing but the enjoyment of the life of this world﴾, that is, all of that is nothing but the enjoyment of the life of this world, which people enjoy and then it passes away and perishes with their passing away. ﴿And the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous﴾, that is, Paradise and what is in it of lasting bounty, for the righteous who believed and guarded themselves against shirk and sins. What is with Allah is better than what is with people, and what remains is better than what perishes. For this reason the wise said: If the world were gold and the Hereafter were clay (*kharaf*, earthenware), the intelligent person would choose the Hereafter over the world, for it is the choice of what remains over what perishes.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The inclination toward this world and the seeking of its enjoyments is innate in man; therefore, if it were given to the disbeliever on account of his disbelief, all people would incline toward it and seek it through disbelief.

2- The lowliness of this world before Allah and the lack of concern for it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If the world were worth the wing of a mosquito before Allah, He would not give a disbeliever a single sip of water from it." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who graded it sound. And in Sahih Muslim: "The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever."

3- A clarification that the Hereafter is better for the righteous.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 43, verses 36–40:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And whoever turns away (ya'shu) from the remembrance of the Most Merciful﴾: that is, he turns away, blind and heedless of the remembrance of the Most Merciful, which is the Qur'an, ignoring it.

﴿We appoint for him a devil﴾: that is, We make for him a devil who accompanies him to mislead and seduce him.

﴿So he is a companion to him﴾: that is, he who is blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful is a companion of Satan.

﴿And indeed they hinder them from the way﴾: that is, the devils who accompany them hinder them from the path of guidance.

﴿And they think that they are guided﴾: that is, those who are blind to the Qur'an, its proofs, and the remembrance of the Most Merciful and obedience to Him think that they are guided, meaning that they are upon the truth and correctness, and this is by the adornment of the companion for them.

﴿As far as the two easts﴾: that is, as much distance as there is between the east and the west. He says this in disavowal of him.

﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you have wronged (yourselves)﴾: that is, it will not benefit you today, O blind ones, since you wronged yourselves with polytheism and sins.

﴿That you, in the punishment, will be sharing﴾: your sharing in the punishment is not beneficial to you.

﴿Then can you make the deaf hear, or guide the blind﴾: that is, you, O our Messenger, cannot make the deaf hear, nor guide the blind, and these people, Allah has made them deaf and blinded their sight, because they turned away from His remembrance.

﴿And whoever is in manifest error﴾: that is, just as you cannot guide whoever is in manifest error, away from the truth and guidance.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in presenting guidance to the astray, by disclosing their states and illuminating the way for them. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful﴾: that is, he turns away, blind and heedless of the remembrance of the Most Merciful, which is the Qur'an, and the worship of the Most Merciful, ignoring that. ﴿We appoint for him a devil﴾: that is, We bring about, as a consequence of his aversion, a devil, and We make him a companion for him who does not part from him in this world or in the Hereafter. ﴿So he is a companion to him, always.﴾ And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed they hinder them from the way, while they think that they are guided﴾: that is, the companions whom He, the Exalted, has appointed, according to His custom in causes and effects, for those blind to His remembrance, hinder them through adorning and beautifying every sin, until they are immersed in every sin, wallow in every falsehood and evil, and stray from the path of guidance and right direction; and yet they think they are guided, while others are the wrongdoers.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Until, when he comes to Us﴾: that is, on the Day of Resurrection. The one blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful says: "Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts," wishing that the distance between him and his companion among the devils were as great as between the east and the west. Allah the Exalted says to those blind ones: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you have wronged yourselves with polytheism and sins in the world; that you, in the punishment, will be sharing﴾: that is, your sharing in the punishment is not beneficial to you, nor will it ever be of any glory. And His saying to His Messenger: ﴿Then can you make the deaf hear, or guide the blind, and whoever is in manifest error?﴾ Allah the Exalted rebukes His Messenger for his supposing that he could guide them by himself without Allah's will for them, since he, ﷺ, was striving in calling them, while they increased in nothing but blindness, heedlessness, and disbelief. So Allah the Exalted addresses His Messenger: ﴿Then can you﴾, the interrogation being for denial: make hear the deaf whom Allah has taken away their hearing, or guide the blind whom Allah has taken away their sight, and whoever is in manifest error away from the truth and the path of right direction and guidance? You cannot do that, so ease your mind and be gentle in your calling, for you are not charged except with conveying, and you have conveyed.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Explanation of Allah's custom regarding one who turns away from the remembrance of Allah: a devil is caused to be assigned to him who misguides him and forever deprives him of guidance, so he persists in sins and wrongdoing, astray from the saved and happy path, while he thinks he is guided. This befalls those who turn away from the Book and the Sunnah, such as innovators, people of whims and desires, and we seek refuge with Allah the Exalted.

2- Sharing in the punishment on the Day of Resurrection does not lighten it.

3- Explanation that whoever Allah has blinded and deafened, according to His custom in that, has no guide, no one to make him hear, and no one to make him see.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 43, verse 46–50:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs﴾: That is, We sent him with the miracles that testify to the truth of his message.

﴿To Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾: That is, and his people from the Copts.

﴿Whereupon they laughed at them﴾: That is, with mockery and derision.

﴿And We showed them no sign except that it was greater than its sister﴾: That is, of the signs of punishment such as the flood, greater than the one preceding it among the signs.

﴿And they said, "O sorcerer"﴾: That is, O you who know sorcery and are deeply versed in it.

﴿By what He has promised you﴾: That is, of removing the punishment from us if we believe.

﴿Indeed, we will be guided﴾: That is, if you remove the punishment from us, we will indeed believe.

﴿Then, when We removed the punishment from them, at once they broke their word﴾: That is, they violated their covenant and did not believe.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And We certainly sent﴾: The recounting of this story here was for two reasons. First, to draw a parallel between the situation of the Quraysh and that of Pharaoh, when the men of Quraysh said, "Why is he not someone of wealth and status, like al-Walid ibn al-Mughira or ʿUrwa ibn Masʿud?" and Pharaoh said, "Am I not better than this one who is contemptible," meaning Moses, peace be upon him. Second, to console the Messenger ﷺ and encourage him to be patient as Moses was patient, and he is one of the five Messengers of firm resolve (ulu al-ʿazm). So He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs﴾, that is, with Our proofs that testify to the truth of Moses in his message to Pharaoh and his people, that they should worship Allah and abandon the worship of others, and that they should send the Children of Israel with Moses so that he could take them to the Promised Land, "Palestine." When he came to them, he said, "I am the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds; I have come to you to command you to worship Allah alone and to abandon the worship of anyone besides Him, for none deserves worship except Allah." They demanded signs as evidence of his claim, and when he brought them the great signs, they met him with laughter, mockery and derision. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿But when he brought them Our signs, behold, they laughed at them﴾.

And His saying: ﴿And We showed them no sign except that it was greater than its sister﴾: that is, We showed Pharaoh and his chiefs no sign except that it was a greater proof of Moses' truthfulness than the one before it. He said: ﴿And We seized them with punishment that they might return﴾ to the truth, believe and affirm the oneness of God. ﴿And they said to Moses, "O sorcerer"﴾, that is, the one who knows sorcery and is deeply versed in it, thinking that the miracles were the work of a sorcerer. ﴿Invoke your Lord for us by what He has promised you; indeed, we will be guided﴾: that is, ask your Lord to lift from us this punishment, such as the flood, the locusts, the lice and the frogs, and we will believe. Whenever the punishment descended upon them, they would ask Moses and promise to believe in him if Allah removed the punishment from them, and each time they would break their word. This is His saying: ﴿Then, when We removed the punishment from them, at once they broke their word﴾, that is, they violated the covenant and did not believe as they had promised.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The signs are evidence of the truth of the one who brings them, but they do not necessarily entail faith on the part of those who witness them.

2. Allah may seize individuals or groups for their sin time after time, so that they may turn back to Him in repentance.

3. The prohibition of breaking promises and violating covenants, and that both are signs and marks of hypocrisy.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 43, verses 51–56:

Explanation of the words:

"And Pharaoh proclaimed among his people": that is, he called out to them, boasting and showing off with what he possessed.

"And these rivers flow beneath me": that is, the Nile flows beneath my palaces.

"Will you not see?": that is, my greatness and the majesty and perfection I possess.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 43, verses 57–62:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example﴾: that is, when Jesus son of Mary is made an example; the one who struck the example was Ibn al-Za'bara.

﴿Behold, your people turn away from it⦆: that is, when the polytheists among your people turn away from it, that is, they laugh, joyful at what they heard.

﴿And they said: "Are our gods better, or is he?"﴾: that is, are our gods whom we worship better, or is he, that is, Jesus son of Mary, so that we would accept our gods being with him?

﴿They cite it to you only for argument's sake﴾: that is, they made the example for you only as a contentious dispute based on falsehood, knowing that the word for non-rational beings does not apply to Jesus, peace be upon him.

﴿Nay, they are a contentious people﴾: that is, they are extremely quarrelsome.

﴿He is only a servant whom We favoured﴾: that is, he is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour with prophethood.

﴿And We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾: that is, his being born without a father made him an example for the Children of Israel, given how strange it was, by which they may infer God's power over whatever He wills.

﴿And if We willed, We would have made angels from among you, succeeding one another on the earth﴾: that is, if He willed, He would have destroyed you and put angels in your place.

﴿on the earth, succeeding﴾: that is, they would populate the earth and worship God in it, succeeding you there after your destruction.

﴿And indeed he is a sign for the Hour﴾: that is, Jesus, peace be upon him, is a sign of the Hour, known by his descent when he descends.

﴿So do not be in doubt about it﴾: that is, do not doubt it, neither as to its occurrence nor its nearness.

﴿And follow Me; this is the straight path﴾: that is, say to them: follow Me in monotheism; this is the straight path, which is Islam.

﴿And let not Satan hinder you﴾: that is, let not Satan turn you away from Islam.

﴿Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾: that is, Satan is to you a manifest enemy, so do not follow him.

Explanation of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾. It is related that Ibn al-Za'bara said to the Messenger of God ﷺ: "When the verse 'Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell; you will be its certain arrivals' was revealed, you said it. Is this for us and our gods, or for all the nations?" The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "It is for you and your gods and for all nations." Ibn al-Za'bara said: "I have defeated you, by the Lord of the Ka'bah! Are not the Christians worshipping the Messiah, the Jews worshipping 'Uzayr, and the Banu Mulayh worshipping the angels? If these are in the Fire, then we are content that we and our gods be with them." The polytheists rejoiced at this and laughed, raising their voices loudly in laughter. In this incident the verse was revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example﴾, that is, when Ibn al-Za'bara made Jesus son of Mary an example, comparing him to the idols, in that the Christians took him as a god and worshipped him besides God. He said: "If Jesus, 'Uzayr and the angels are in the Fire, then we are content that we and our gods be with them." The polytheists rejoiced at this, turned away, and raised their voices in laughter. They said: "Are our gods better, or is he?" meaning the Messiah. God said to His Messenger: ﴿They cite it to you only for argument's sake﴾, that is, Ibn al-Za'bara did not cite this example seeking the truth or inquiring into it, but he cited it for you only for the sake of dispute and quarrel. ﴿Nay, they are a contentious people﴾, naturally disposed to dispute and contention.

His saying: ﴿He is only a servant whom We favoured﴾, that is, Jesus is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour with prophethood and messengerhood, and ﴿We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾, by which they infer the power of God, may He be mighty and majestic, over all that He wills, for He created him without a father just as He created Adam from dust, then said to him "Be," and he was.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if We willed, We would have made angels from among you, succeeding one another on the earth﴾, that is, if We willed, We would have destroyed you, O children of Adam, and not left one of you, and We would have put angels in your place on the earth, succeeding you there, populating it, worshipping God in it, affirming His oneness, and not associating anything with Him.

His saying: ﴿And indeed he is a sign for the Hour﴾, that is, Jesus, peace be upon him, is a sign of the Hour: his descent at the end of time is a sign of the Hour's nearness. ﴿So do not be in doubt about it﴾, that is, do not doubt its coming, for it is coming and near. His saying: ﴿And follow Me﴾, that is, say to them, O our Messenger: follow Me in monotheism and in the guidance I brought you; ﴿this is the straight path﴾, that is, Islam, founded on monotheism, which the Qur'an came down with and which the Messenger of God ﷺ brought. ﴿And let not Satan hinder you from Islam﴾ with his whisperings and seduction, turning you away from monotheism and Islam: ﴿Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾. Nothing demonstrates his enmity more than that he expelled Adam from the Garden through his seduction, out of envy of him and transgression against him. Such an enemy must never be listened to, nor followed, nor have his footsteps trodden. Whoever follows his footsteps will perish.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification that the Quraysh were given skill in disputation and strength in contention.

2- Condemnation of disputation not aimed at establishing truth and refuting falsehood; and in the hadith: "No people go astray after being guided to something but they are given to disputation."

3- The nobility of Jesus and the exalted rank he holds, and that his descent to earth is one of the major signs of the Hour's nearness.

4- Affirmation of resurrection and recompense.

5- The prohibition of following Satan, for he leads astray and does not guide.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if We willed, We would have made angels from among you, succeeding one another on the earth﴾, that is, if We willed, We would have destroyed you, O children of Adam, and not left one of you, and We would have put angels in your place on the earth, succeeding you there, populating it, worshipping God in it, affirming His oneness, and not associating anything with Him.

His saying: ﴿And indeed he is a sign for the Hour﴾, that is, Jesus, peace be upon him, is a sign of the Hour: his descent at the end of time is a sign of the Hour's nearness. ﴿So do not be in doubt about it﴾, that is, do not doubt its coming, for it is coming and near. His saying: ﴿And follow Me﴾, that is, say to them, O our Messenger: follow Me in monotheism and in the guidance I brought you; ﴿this is the straight path﴾, that is, Islam, founded on monotheism, which the Qur'an came down with and which the Messenger of God ﷺ brought. ﴿And let not Satan hinder you from Islam﴾ with his whisperings and seduction, turning you away from monotheism and Islam: ﴿Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾. Nothing demonstrates his enmity more than that he expelled Adam from the Garden through his seduction, out of envy of him and transgression against him. Such an enemy must never be listened to, nor followed, nor have his footsteps trodden. Whoever follows his footsteps will perish.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification that the Quraysh were given skill in disputation and strength in contention.

2- Condemnation of disputation not aimed at establishing truth and refuting falsehood; and in the hadith: "No people go astray after being guided to something but they are given to disputation."

3- The nobility of Jesus and the exalted rank he holds, and that his descent to earth is one of the major signs of the Hour's nearness.

4- Affirmation of resurrection and recompense.

5- The prohibition of following Satan, for he leads astray and does not guide.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 43, verses 63–66:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And when Jesus came with clear proofs﴾: That is, when Jesus son of Mary came to the Children of Israel with miracles and laws.

﴿He said, "I have come to you with wisdom"﴾: That is, he said to the Children of Israel, "I have come to you with prophethood and the laws of the Gospel."

﴿And to make clear to you some of that about which you differ﴾: That is, I have come to clarify for you what you have differed about from the rulings of the Torah, concerning matters of religion and other things.

﴿So fear Allah and obey me﴾: That is, fear Allah and obey me in what I convey to you from Allah of commands and prohibitions.

﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him﴾: That is, indeed Allah is my God and your God, so worship Him with love of Him, glorification of Him, and humility before Him.

﴿This is a straight path﴾: That is, the fear of Allah, obedience to the Messenger, and worship of Allah according to what He has legislated, which is Islam, expressed as the straight path.

﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾: That is, concerning the matter of Jesus: is he God, or the son of God, or the third of three?

﴿So woe to those who wronged from the punishment of a painful day﴾: That is, woe to those who disbelieved because of what they said about Jesus of falsehood and lies.

﴿Do they await except the Hour, that it will come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive?﴾: That is, what do these factions await, while they persist in what they said about Jesus, except the Hour coming upon them suddenly, unexpectedly, while they are unaware.

Meaning of the verses:

After Allah mentioned the disputation of the polytheists of Makkah and their delight in the falsehood that Ibn al-Za'bara said concerning the angels, Ezra and Jesus (peace be upon them), namely that they would be in the Fire along with those they worshipped, Allah cleared the angels, Ezra and Jesus, because they had not commanded people to worship them so that they would be held accountable for it; rather, it was Satan who commanded worship of them, so Satan and those who worshipped them are the ones in the Fire. Allah mentioned the honour and station of Jesus, that he is a servant upon whom He bestowed prophethood, and made him an example for the Children of Israel by which they might take proof of Allah's power, since He created him without a father just as He created Adam without a father or a mother, and created him only from dust. He mentioned the messengership of Jesus (peace be upon him) to the Children of Israel so that this would be an admonition to the disbelievers of Makkah. So Allah said: ﴿And when Jesus came with clear proofs﴾, that is, he came to the Children of Israel accompanied by clear proofs, which are the Gospel and miracles such as bringing the dead to life, healing the blind and the leper, and the like. He said to them, ﴿I have come to you with wisdom﴾, that is, prophethood from Allah; ﴿and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ﴾ from the rulings of the Torah and matters [of religion]. ﴿So fear Allah, O Children of Israel﴾, that is, fear His punishment which follows from His disobedience, ﴿and obey me in what I convey to you of commands and prohibitions from Allah.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord﴾, that is, my God and your God; there is no god but Him, so worship Him by doing what He loves and abandoning what angers Him, out of love for Him, glorification of Him, awe, and hope. As for His saying ﴿This is a straight path﴾, that is, what I have called you to, namely fearing Allah, obeying His Messenger, and worshipping Him alone, is the straight path that leads its follower to the happiness of both abodes. Allah said: ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾, that is, from among the Children of Israel, Jews and Christians. A group of the Jews said, as a lie and fabrication, that Jesus son of Mary was the son of adultery and his mother was an adulteress, and they said he was a sorcerer.

The Christians said: he is God, or the son of God, or the third of three.

Allah said: ﴿So woe to those who wronged from the punishment of a painful day﴾, that is, painful. The Lord threatened them with woe, which is a valley flowing in Hell with what gathers from the pus of the private parts and bodies of the people of the Fire, of blood, sores and filth; and it is the painful punishment of the Day of Resurrection. He threatened these wrongdoers because of what they said about Jesus, the servant of Allah and His Messenger (peace be upon him). And Allah said: ﴿Do they await except the Hour﴾, that is, they await nothing but the Hour, because they have not repented to Allah nor returned to the truth concerning what they said about Jesus; rather they persisted: the Jews describe him with the basest attributes, and the Christians describe him with divinity, which is the right of Allah, the Lord of Jesus and the Lord of the worlds, ﴿that it will come upon them suddenly﴾, that is, unexpectedly, ﴿while they do not perceive,﴾ because they are preoccupied with the atom, hydrogen, colonialism, trade, and immersion in desires, as is the reality and what is witnessed today. And Allah the Mighty has spoken truly.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Clarification of Jesus's messengership to the Children of Israel.

2- The obligation of piety toward Allah and obedience to the Messenger, and monotheism in worship of Allah.

3- Clarification of the evil of disagreement, and what it drags along of deep immersion in disbelief and corruption.

4- Allah's warning to the Jews and Christians who did not enter Islam: woe, which is the painful punishment of a day.
