Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 43, verse 67–73:

Explanation of the words:

"Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the God-fearing": that is, loved ones on the day when the Hour comes upon them suddenly.

"Except the God-fearing": for their love endures for them, because it was for the sake of God and His obedience.

"O My servants, no fear shall be upon you this Day, nor shall you grieve": that is, they will be called, and it will be said to them, "No fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve; rather, you will be made joyful (tuhbaruna), that is, gladdened and honoured."

"There will be passed around to them platters of gold": that is, the angels will go around to them with bowls of gold containing food, and cups of gold containing delicious drink.

"And therein is whatever the souls desire, and delightful to the eyes": that is, in Paradise is whatever the souls desire, enjoying it, and what the eyes find delight in by looking at it.

"And that is Paradise, which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do": that is, it will be said to them, "And this is the Paradise which God has bequeathed to you for your righteous deeds, which are the fruit of your sincere faith and your complete sincerity."

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with mention of the events of the Hour. The Exalted said: "Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the God-fearing." That is, when the Hour comes, the close friends of the worldly life, that is, the loved ones, on the day the Hour comes upon them, will be enemies to one another. That friendship and affection will be cut off and turned into hostility, because it was based on disobedience to God the Exalted. His saying "except the God-fearing" means those who, by doing His commands and abstaining from His prohibitions, fear God the Mighty and Majestic. Their affection and friendship will not be cut off, because it was love for the sake of God, and what is for God endures and continues, while what is for other than God ends and is severed. Their Lord calls to them with His saying: "O My servants, no fear shall be upon you this Day, nor shall you grieve." He describes them with His saying: "Those who believed in Our signs" — that is, in the Qur'an — "and were Muslims," that is, submissive to God outwardly and inwardly. And He says to them: "Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, made joyful." That is, you and your believing wives will rejoice and be gladdened.

His saying: "There will be passed around to them" is an explanation of the bliss of Paradise with which they are blessed: that platters of gold will be passed around to them, which are bowls, containing the most delicious and appealing food, and also cups of gold containing the most delicious drink. "Cups" is the plural of "kub," which is a vessel without a handle or spout, so that one can drink from it from any side. "And therein is whatever the souls desire" of all kinds of pleasures, "and delightful to the eyes" of all kinds of sights. It will be said to them: "You will have therein whatever you desire, and you will abide therein forever; you will not be removed from it, nor will you die therein."

His saying: "And that is Paradise" means: this is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit for the righteous deeds and good works you used to do. As for the sense of inheritance: God the Exalted created for every person two dwellings, one in Paradise and the second in the Fire. Whoever enters Paradise inherits the dwelling of one who entered the Fire; this is the meaning of inheritance. The "bi" in "for what you used to do" is causal, meaning: because of your righteous deeds, which purified your souls and cleansed your spirits, so you deserved to enter Paradise and inherit its dwellings.

His saying: "For you therein is abundant fruit, from which you will eat" means that it will be said to them this as an honour and a blessing.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Every friendship on the Day of Resurrection will be cut off, except a friendship that was for God and by God, so affection in this world should be for God and not for other than Him, the Exalted.

2- An explanation of the excellence of piety and the nobility of the God-fearing, who guard against shirk and sins.

3- An explanation that God gathers a man with his Muslim wife in Paradise.

4- An explanation of the bliss of the people of Paradise: food, drink, and all kinds of delights.

5- Faith and righteous deeds are a cause for entering Paradise, just as shirk and sins are a cause for entering the Fire.

1- Every friendship on the Day of Resurrection will be cut off, except a friendship that was for God and by God, so affection in this world should be for God and not for other than Him, the Exalted.

**Explanation of the words:**

*Indeed, the criminals are in the punishment of Hell*: That is, those who committed crimes against themselves through polytheism (shirk) and disobedience will abide forever in Hell, not leaving it and not dying.

*The punishment will not be lightened for them, and they will be in it in despair*: That is, the punishment will not be eased for them, and they will be silent in it, a silence of despair.

*And they will call, "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us"*: That is, they will call out to Malik, the keeper of the Fire, saying to him, "Let your Lord cause us to die."

*He will say, "Indeed, you will remain."*: That is, he answered them after a thousand years had passed since their call, saying, "Indeed, you will remain," meaning you will abide in the punishment of Hell forever.

*Indeed, We brought you the truth, but most of you are averse to the truth*: That is, the reason for your remaining is that We brought you the truth through Our Messenger, and the truth is monotheism and the worship of God in the manner He prescribed; but most of you disliked the truth.

*Or have they determined a matter? Then indeed We are determining*: That is, they resolved to plot against the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), so We are determining Our plan for their destruction.

*And Our messengers are with them, writing*: That is, Our angels, the recording guardians, write down what they conceal and what they disclose.

**Meaning of the verses:**

When God mentioned Paradise and its bliss, in these verses He mentioned the Fire and its punishment. This is the combination of encouragement and warning that characterizes the Qur'anic method of calling to God and guiding people to reform. God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the criminals﴾, that is, those who committed crimes against themselves, corrupting their souls through polytheism and disobedience, are in the punishment of Hell, abiding forever. The punishment will not be lightened for them, that is, it will not be eased, and they will be in it, that is, in the punishment, silent and despairing, hopeless. And God the Exalted said: "We did not wrong them by punishing them with this torment, but they were the wrongdoers," since they corrupted themselves with polytheism and disobedience.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they will call, "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us"﴾: He informs that the people of that everlasting punishment, which is not lightened, called out to Malik, the keeper of the Fire, and said to him, "Let your Lord cause us to die, so that we may rest from the punishment." Malik answered them after a thousand years, saying: "Indeed, you will remain," that is, in the punishment of Hell. He gave the reason for this ruling, that they would remain forever, saying: ﴿Indeed, We brought you the truth﴾, that is, We sent to you Our Messenger with the truth, calling you to it, which is faith and righteous deeds that purify the souls. But most of you disliked that, so you did not believe and did not do righteous deeds, preferring the pleasures of this world over the Hereafter; so you died in the Hereafter upon polytheism and disbelief. This is the recompense of the disbelievers.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or have they determined a matter? Then indeed We are determining﴾: That is, rather, these polytheists determined a matter by which they plotted against the Messenger and his call. If they did so, then indeed We are determining, that is, We are firmly resolving a matter that adds to them, namely their punishment, and the nullification of what they firmly resolved of plotting against the Messenger and his call. And His saying: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private counsel? Yes﴾: We do hear that, and Our messengers, who are the recording guardians, are with them, writing what they say, in secret and openly. It is narrated that three men said, while they were beneath the curtains of the Ka'bah, one of them said, "Do you think God hears our speech?" One of them said, "If you speak aloud, He hears; if you speak secretly, He does not hear." The second said, "If He hears when you declare, then He hears when you speak secretly." So this was revealed: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private counsel? Yes﴾, meaning, We hear their secret and their private counsel.

**Guidance of the verses:**

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Clarification of the punishment for crime against the self through polytheism and disobedience.

2- The punishment of the Hereafter cannot be endured and cannot be measured; this is shown by their asking for death to rest from it, while they will not die.

3- The greatest factor in the dislike of truth is love of this world and bestial desires for food, drink, and sexual relations; these make religion and its laws hateful to their possessor, laws which may restrain excess in these things.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 43, verses 81–85:

Explanation of the words:

"Qul in kana lil-Rahmani walad" (Say: If the Most Merciful had a son): That is, say, O our Messenger, to these polytheists who claim that the angels are daughters of God: if the Most Merciful had a son, supposing it to be so.

"Fa-ana awwalu al-'abidin" (Then I am the first of the worshippers): That is, then I would be the first to worship him, out of exaltation and reverence for God. But He has no son, so there is no worship due to anyone other than Him.

"Subhana Rabbi al-samawati" (Glory be to the Lord of the heavens): That is, He is exalted and sanctified.

"'Amma yasifun" (above what they describe): That is, above what they ascribe to God Most High, namely that He has a son and partners.

"Fa-dharhum yakhudu wa yal'abu" (So leave them to plunge into falsehood and play): That is, leave them, O our Messenger, to plunge into their falsehood and to play in their worldly life.

"Wa Huwa alladhi fi al-sama'i ilah" (He is the one who is God in the heaven): That is, the one worshipped in the heaven.

"Wa fi al-ardi ilah" (And God on the earth): That is, and worshipped on the earth.

"Wa tabaraka alladhi lahu mulku al-samawati" (Blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens): That is, exalted and magnified is the majesty of the One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens.

"Wa 'indahu 'ilmu al-sa'ah" (And with Him is the knowledge of the Hour): That is, with Him is the knowledge of the time of its coming.

Meaning of the verses:

God Most High had previously rebuked the polytheists for their claim that the angels are daughters of God, and threatened them with punishment for their false saying. Here He told His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to them, if the Most Merciful had a son as you fabricate, supposing and assuming it, then I would be the first of the worshippers of Him; but the Most Merciful has no son, so I would not worship other than God Most High. This is what is indicated by His saying: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾. And His saying: ﴿Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above what they describe﴾: He, Most High, declared Himself exalted and sanctified, for He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and the Lord of the Throne, that is, the Owner of all of that and its sovereignty over all of it, above what the polytheists describe Him with, namely that He has a son and partners.

Here God Most High said to His Messenger: if they persist in their falsehood of polytheism, and in their fabrication against God, then leave them to plunge into their falsehood and to play in their worldly life, until they meet their Day which they are promised, which is the day of their prepared punishment, and that is the Day of Resurrection.

As for His saying: ﴿And He is the one who is God in the heaven and God on the earth﴾: that is, worshipped in the heaven and worshipped on the earth, meaning the one held in supreme reverence, loved with utmost love, and humbled before with utmost humility, in earth and heaven. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 43, verses 86–89:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And those whom they invoke besides Him⦆ — that is, they worship them.

"Besides Him" — that is, besides Allah.

"Intercession" — that is, for anyone.

"Except those who bear witness to the truth" — that is, but the one who bears witness to the truth, affirming the oneness of Allah the Exalted with knowledge; this is the one who will receive the intercession of the angels and the prophets.

"So how are they turned away?" — that is, how are they diverted from the truth after knowing it?

"And his saying" — that is, the saying of the Prophet: "O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe."

"So turn away from them" — that is, disregard them.

"And say, 'Peace.' But they will come to know" — that is, my command is: peace from you; but they will soon know the outcome of their disbelief.

Meaning of the verses:

When the Exalted informed us in the previous verse that people will return to Him on the Day of Resurrection, and the polytheists claimed that their deities, including the angels and others, would intercede for them, and used this as a pretext for worshipping them, the Exalted informed them in this verse [86] that those whom they invoke, meaning worship, among idols, angels and others besides Allah, do not possess intercession for anyone. Allah alone possesses intercession and bestows it upon whomever He wills. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿None possess the power of intercession, except those who bear witness to the truth, and they know﴾... that is, Allah excepted whoever bears witness to the truth, namely that there is no god but Allah, and knows this with certain knowledge. Such a person may be interceded for by the angels or the prophets. Hence He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿except those who bear witness to the truth, and they know﴾, meaning they know in their hearts what they testify to with their tongues. Thus the monotheists will receive intercession by the permission of Allah the Exalted. As for His saying: ﴿And if you asked them﴾, that is, if you asked these polytheists who created them, they would answer, "Allah." Glory be to Allah, how do they acknowledge the Lordship of Allah in His oneness and yet deny the oneness of worship? Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿So how are they turned away?﴾, that is, how are they diverted from the truth after knowing it? They recognise that Allah is the Creator of them, yet they worship other than Him and abandon His worship.

As for His saying: ﴿And his saying, "O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe"﴾, that is, Allah knows the saying of His Messenger and his complaint, which is: "O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe," because he witnessed their obstinacy and stubbornness, and he complained to his Lord the Exalted. His Lord, mighty and majestic, commanded him to pardon them, that is, to overlook the harm and hardship he suffers from them, and to say to them, "Peace," which is a peace of disengagement, not a greeting of honour and respect. That is, say to them: "My command is peace." ﴿But they will come to know﴾: this persistence in disbelief and denial is a warning to them, mentioning the painful punishment awaiting them if they die in their disbelief.

Lessons from the verses:

1. No one possesses intercession on the Day of Resurrection except Allah the Exalted. Whoever He permits intercedes, and whoever He does not permit does not intercede. Intercession is granted only to the people of monotheism, and there is no intercession for the people of polytheism and disbelief.

2. The polytheists of the Arabs at the time of the Prophethood acknowledged the Lordship of Allah but were polytheists in worship.

3. The legitimacy of pardon and forgiveness when unable to establish the prescribed punishments and to exalt the word of Allah the Exalted.

As for His saying: ﴿And his saying, "O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe"﴾, that is, Allah knows the saying of His Messenger and his complaint, which is: "O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe," because he witnessed their obstinacy and stubbornness, and he complained to his Lord the Exalted. His Lord, mighty and majestic, commanded him to pardon them, that is, to overlook the harm and hardship he suffers from them, and to say to them, "Peace," which is a peace of disengagement, not a greeting of honour and respect. That is, say to them: "My command is peace." ﴿But they will come to know﴾: this persistence in disbelief and denial is a warning to them, mentioning the painful punishment awaiting them if they die in their disbelief.

Lessons from the verses:

1. No one possesses intercession on the Day of Resurrection except Allah the Exalted. Whoever He permits intercedes, and whoever He does not permit does not intercede. Intercession is granted only to the people of monotheism, and there is no intercession for the people of polytheism and disbelief.

2. The polytheists of the Arabs at the time of the Prophethood acknowledged the Lordship of Allah but were polytheists in worship.

3. The legitimacy of pardon and forgiveness when unable to establish the prescribed punishments and to exalt the word of Allah the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 43, verses 86–89:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And those whom they invoke besides Him⦆ — that is, they worship them.

"Besides Him" — that is, besides Allah.

"Intercession" — that is, for anyone.

"Except those who bear witness to the truth" — that is, but the one who bears witness to the truth, affirming the oneness of Allah the Exalted with knowledge; this is the one who will receive the intercession of the angels and the prophets.

"So how are they turned away?" — that is, how are they diverted from the truth after knowing it?

"And his saying" — that is, the saying of the Prophet: "O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe."

"So turn away from them" — that is, disregard them.

"And say, 'Peace.' But they will come to know" — that is, my command is: peace from you; but they will soon know the outcome of their disbelief.

Meaning of the verses:

When the Exalted informed us in the previous verse that people will return to Him on the Day of Resurrection, and the polytheists claimed that their deities, including the angels and others, would intercede for them, and used this as a pretext for worshipping them, the Exalted informed them in this verse [86] that those whom they invoke, meaning worship, among idols, angels and others besides Allah, do not possess intercession for anyone. Allah alone possesses intercession and bestows it upon whomever He wills. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿None possess the power of intercession, except those who bear witness to the truth, and they know﴾... that is, Allah excepted whoever bears witness to the truth, namely that there is no god but Allah, and knows this with certain knowledge. Such a person may be interceded for by the angels or the prophets. Hence He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿except those who bear witness to the truth, and they know﴾, meaning they know in their hearts what they testify to with their tongues. Thus the monotheists will receive intercession by the permission of Allah the Exalted. As for His saying: ﴿And if you asked them﴾, that is, if you asked these polytheists who created them, they would answer, "Allah." Glory be to Allah, how do they acknowledge the Lordship of Allah in His oneness and yet deny the oneness of worship? Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿So how are they turned away?﴾, that is, how are they diverted from the truth after knowing it? They recognise that Allah is the Creator of them, yet they worship other than Him and abandon His worship.

As for His saying: ﴿And his saying, "O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe"﴾, that is, Allah knows the saying of His Messenger and his complaint, which is: "O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe," because he witnessed their obstinacy and stubbornness, and he complained to his Lord the Exalted. His Lord, mighty and majestic, commanded him to pardon them, that is, to overlook the harm and hardship he suffers from them, and to say to them, "Peace," which is a peace of disengagement, not a greeting of honour and respect. That is, say to them: "My command is peace." ﴿But they will come to know﴾: this persistence in disbelief and denial is a warning to them, mentioning the painful punishment awaiting them if they die in their disbelief.
